description_en: This site contains archaeological artefacts from the 12th-15th century centuries that have been placed on a small platform along the path leading to the village of Sahubada. Stone lions sculptures and architectural remains are among the artefacts. They attest the presence of significant monuments in the past, confirming the predominant role of the Sahubada area as a seat of power during the Khaśa Malla era (12th-14th century) and under the Kalyāl dynasty of Jumla, who succeeded the latter (Andolfatto 2019).According to unpublished data collected by French-Swiss archaeologist D. Baudais and D.R. Sharma (Sharma 2012:178-9), the site contains four stone lions (or tigers, according to D. R. Sharma). In 2022 CE, only three lions were found in situ. The missing one is probably laying around in nearby bushes. A small shed built to the north-east of the platform houses a large stoneāmalakaand akalaśa. These elements attest the presence of now-goneśikharatemples (at least one).
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université. Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
